chunks: Inductor and capacitor cycle in PFM. The question: Describe the charge/discharge cycle of inductor and capacitor.
In PFM, one cycle has three parts. First the converter sleeps while the output capacitor alone feeds the load and the output sags.
Then a pulse of inductor current ramps up and down and refills the capacitor. Then the converter sleeps again.
Over a full period, the charge put in equals the charge the load takes out.
Think of a bank account that pays your bills continuously. Money leaves at a steady rate, so the balance slowly falls.
When it hits a floor, you make one deposit of a fixed size, and the balance jumps back up.
The account is the capacitor, the bills are the load, and the deposit is one pulse from the inductor.
The analogy falls short in that a deposit does not appear instantly: it rises and falls over about a microsecond.

"Asleep, the capacitor feeds the load and the output droops.
When it hits the threshold, the high-side FET turns on, the inductor current ramps up and stores energy; once it exceeds the load current the capacitor charges.
Then the low side takes over, the inductor releases its energy into the output as the current ramps down, and the capacitor keeps charging until the inductor current drops below the load.
At zero current everything turns off and the capacitor discharges into the load until the next pulse. Net charge per period is zero."
